text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson's Virgin Group plans to launch a 24-hour telephone banking operation that aims to take a slice of business from major British banks, The Times reported Monday.

It said the backer behind Virgin's latest ambitious foray into financial services, after tackling directly-sold insurance and investment products, was Australian Mutual Provident (AMP), the insurance giant.

The Times said Virgin will be targeting well paid professionals in their thirties and forties who are fed up with their existing bank service. The launch has been penciled in for early 1998 and pilot plans are expected later this year.
Virgin's service will compete with HSBC Holdings' highly successful telephone banking subsidiary First Direct, which has attracted many disaffected customers.
Virgin plans to follow by also targeting customers of National Westminster Bank Plc, Barclays Plc, Lloyds TSB Group Plc and Midland Bank, the report said.
The Times report quoted Tony Wood, Virgin's marketing director, as saying: "This is a major new venture for us in the financial services market."
